versions.localizedDescription:
The first release of Sonic Free Riders for iPhone and iPad.

**No game content is included.** You need your own *Sonic Free Riders (USA, Europe)* Xbox 360 disc image or the disc's files.

## Install

1. Install `SonicFreeRiders-iOS-1.0.0.ipa` with AltStore, SideStore, Sideloadly, ESign or TrollStore.
2. Copy your disc image or folder to the device, open the app, choose **Install from a disc image or folder**, and pick it.
3. Press **Start game**.

Needs an A15 Bionic or newer and iOS 15 or later. See the README (https://github.com/DevZer0D4Y/SonicFreeRiders-iOS#readme) for controls and settings.

## What's in it

- Full races at 60 fps on recent iPhones; on slower devices races keep real time by drawing fewer frames.
- Touch controls for every race action (left stick, A/B/X/Y, LB/RB, RT, right stick, START), tilt to steer, and MFi, Xbox and PlayStation controllers.
- The race map lines up with the racers on wide phone screens.
- Racers no longer fall short on Dolphin Resort's big jump or fall out of Metropolis Speedway when frames are skipped.
- The launcher scrolls with a swipe and keeps its layout after switching apps.

Based on Free Riders Recompiled (https://github.com/YuutaTsubasa/Free-Riders-Recompiled) by YuutaTsubasa.

SHA-256 of the IPA: `b64947df0aadc9aa00322ae74039f045f07c11a848feab44bde4380e4335da6d`

Source code, game-file requirements and instructions: https://github.com/DevZer0D4Y/TheChoicerVoicer-iOS

versions.localizedDescription:
## 1.0.0

First iOS release, for The Choicer Voicer versions made with Godot 4.0 to 4.4 (tested with 0.5.1).

**The game is not included.** Buy it from YeahMaybe on itch.io (https://yeahmaybe.itch.io/the-choicer-voicer), then copy the Windows version's `.exe` into **Files → On My iPhone → The Choicer Voicer** and reopen the app.

- Runs the game from your own `.exe` or `.pck`, read straight from the file.
- Microphone input works on iOS, with the permission requested at launch.
- Full screen on every iPhone and iPad, in either landscape orientation; dub mode's TV and remote keep their PC layout and pack videos keep their proportions.
- Two-finger tap as right click.
- The game's "open folder" buttons open the folder in the Files app.
- Packs, recordings and saves in the app's folder in the Files app.

Known issues: the 3D studio's lighting is flatter than on PC (no VoxelGI on Godot's Mobile renderer), and versions of the game made with Godot 4.5 or later don't load yet.

Install: sign and install the IPA with ESign, AltStore, SideStore or Sideloadly. Needs iOS 15+.

Unofficial fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by YeahMaybe. Apart from the game's logo as its icon, it contains no part of the game; it must not be sold.

versions.localizedDescription:
First release of Unreal Tournament 3 for iPhone and iPad.

**No game content is included: you need your own Xbox 360 copy of Unreal Tournament 3.**

## How to play

1. Download `UT3-iOS.ipa` below.
2. Install it with AltStore, SideStore, Sideloadly, ESign or TrollStore (the IPA is unsigned; the tool signs it).
3. Dump your own Unreal Tournament 3 disc to an ISO/XISO and put it in the Files app.
4. Open UT3, tap **Choose ISO** and pick the image. It is checked, then copied into the app (a few minutes).
5. Play with a Bluetooth controller (Xbox, PlayStation, MFi) or the on-screen controls, which hide while a controller is connected.

## Requirements

- iPhone or iPad with an A15 Bionic or newer, iOS 15 or later.
- The region-free Xbox 360 disc (English, French, German, Spanish, Italian). Other releases with a different game executable are detected and refused.
- Free space for the disc image.

## Notes

- Up to 60 FPS, with a steady 30 FPS fallback when the device cannot keep up (a warm phone, heavy scenes).
- The first matches can stutter while effects are prepared for the GPU; later sessions are smoother.
- Settings are in `ut3.toml` in the app's folder in Files. See the README for details.

SHA-256 of `UT3-iOS.ipa`: `1140f82eea83e8595bdb96dda0fe997d4a0a91dbee14d7b9acabd64e487b4feb`

Native iOS and Windows ports of SSF2T, UMK3, Slam 'n Jam 96 and THPS2

Source code, game-file requirements and instructions: https://github.com/DevZer0D4Y/NativePorts

versions.marketingVersion: NativePorts 0.4.6 — Arcade Showtime, iPhone speed and audio
versions.localizedDescription:
NBA Showtime now uses the arcade/MAME edition on iOS and Windows, replacing the previous PlayStation edition. Import your own nbashowt.zip and matching nbashowt.chd; game data is not included.

Showtime iPhone changes:
- Move emulation off the UI thread and pace it using a monotonic deadline.
- Batch two signature-checked MIPS polling/copy loops while preserving guest cycles, RAM semantics and interrupt boundaries.
- Bound queued audio latency; fade starvation/recovery and transition across dropped audio to reduce crackles.
- Reduce CRT drawable workload under thermal pressure. CRT remains on by default and can be toggled.

Includes all pending source changes for the other four ports, including their rendering, camera, CRT and version-resource updates.

Downloads:
- SSF2T 0.4.2, UMK3 0.4.2, Slam n Jam 96 0.4.2, THPS2 0.4.3, NBA Showtime 0.4.6 unsigned iOS IPAs.
- NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip contains all five Windows builds and required DLLs.
- SHA256SUMS.txt provides download checksums. IPAs require signing before installation.

Validation: iOS and Windows builds passed; 15,000 randomized MIPS-loop comparisons passed with sanitizers; audio, worker-thread, game import, rendering and camera regression tests passed. The latest separate Showtime iPhone test build was reported to run well by the device owner. Sustained coverage of every scene and physical four-player testing remain pending. Showtime arcade widescreen projection is not implemented; native arcade proportions are retained.

versions.marketingVersion: NativePorts 0.3.0 — NBA Showtime and rendering fixes
versions.localizedDescription:
NBA Showtime (PlayStation USA) joins the four existing ports. All five iOS apps and Windows executables are version 0.3.0.

Changes:
- SSF2T: fixed 512-column widescreen output prevents camera-dependent resizing. Unsupported stage edges are clipped inside the fixed canvas and filled with colored margins; scenery is not mirrored.
- Slam 'n Jam '96: extend the SLES-00076 game's crowd/court clipping checks, rather than only widening the GPU canvas. Original interior pixels and HUD are preserved. No coin prompts; Restart Game remains the console action.
- UMK3: extend solid background/gradient clears into the extra columns before drawing foreground scenery, fixing the rectangular gap reproduced in Scorpion's Lair.
- THPS2: keep the gameplay HUD in the centered original 4:3 area. Increase the normal follow-camera offset by 25% through a guarded boot-time instruction patch, verified on the USA executable. Black letterbox bars and CRT toggle are retained.
- NBA Showtime: supplied PlayStation USA BIN support, four-player multitap, Hangtime-style controls/UI, centered HUD and expanded gameplay canvas, CRT enabled by default with on/off controls.
- Include THPS2's Windows C++ runtime DLLs and version all five builds consistently.

Downloads:
- NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip: all five Windows games. Extract it and keep every DLL beside its EXE.
- Five unsigned IPAs: sign with your sideloading tool. Keep existing bundle identifiers to preserve app data.
- SHA256SUMS.txt: checksums for the downloadable builds.

Game files and signing credentials are not included. NBA Showtime needs the extracted raw PlayStation MODE2/2352 BIN named nbashowt.bin, not its archive or an arcade ROM.

Validation: all ten platform builds passed; Apple/SDL virtual-controller tests, shader compilation, texture-cache checks, rendering helper regressions and local gameplay captures passed. Local captures covered SSF2T camera limits, Slam court pans, UMK3 Scorpion's Lair, THPS2 Hangar, and NBA Showtime gameplay/toggle/HUD. This is not complete stage coverage or physical iPhone/Windows multiplayer validation. THPS2 iOS still uses the CPU interpreter; this release does not claim a verified frame-rate improvement. Some Slam camera angles can still reveal the finite arena's dark exterior.

versions.localizedDescription:
SSF2T and Slam n Jam 0.2.2

iOS and Windows builds passed. iOS IPAs are unsigned; sign/install with ESign, keeping the existing bundle identifiers.

Slam n Jam: startup asks for keyboard 1 or controller Start, with no coin prompt. Restart reads RESTART GAME. PS1 Select is available as Select (keyboard Tab, controller View); old settings migrate. Native gameplay canvas expands from 320 to 426 columns instead of stretching. Original-size sprites, text and HUD remain centered; textures live in original VRAM and expanded framebuffers use separate banks. CRT behavior is unchanged.

SSF2T: reflected edge artwork removed. The visible gameplay window narrows symmetrically as the camera approaches finite stage boundaries, returning to the original 384 columns at either limit. It expands away from those limits. Menus keep their original proportions centered in a 512-column frame with colored sides.

Validation: iOS and Windows builds, controller suite, canvas isolation and stage-boundary tests passed. Real Slam gameplay toggled 320 -> 426 -> 320 columns; all 81,920 pixels of the central original view matched the same saved frame exactly. Real SSF2T gameplay captures returned to 384 columns at both edges, and menu captures were 512 columns with colored margins. Device-specific iPhone and Windows gameplay still needs retesting.

No game files or game screenshots are included. SSF2T and Slam n Jam are version 0.2.2. The unchanged THPS2 and UMK3 version 0.2.1 builds are also included here. Download NativePorts-Windows-x64.zip for all four current Windows builds; the smaller SSF2T-SlamJam96 ZIP contains only those two games. BUILD-VERSIONS.txt inside the complete ZIP identifies every game version.

THPS2 now has a direct CRT ON/OFF button during iPhone gameplay, black top/bottom letterbox bars on iOS and Windows, and a renderer adjustment to keep flat HUD overlays in the central 4:3 area. The iOS CPU interpreter also has a faster RAM instruction-fetch path.

Slam ’n Jam widescreen projection now runs before guest clipping and preserves native sprite/text rendering. SSF2T extends finite scenery edges with mirrored backgrounds while preserving sprite priority. UMK3 extends mixed background tile bands with safeguards for unrelated props.

### Downloads

- Four unsigned iOS IPAs: sign and install using ESign.
- Windows x64 ZIP: contains all four games and required SDL libraries.
- SHA256SUMS.txt: checksums for the downloadable builds.

Existing bundle identifiers are preserved. Game files are not included. NBA Showtime remains unfinished and is not included.

### Validation and remaining checks

All four iOS and Windows builds passed. Controller, VRAM, GTE projection and stage-edge regression checks passed; 92 Dreamcast shader variants compiled and linked. A local Slam ’n Jam gameplay capture showed complete crowd rendering in one tested camera.

THPS2 iPhone frame-rate improvement and HUD placement still need device confirmation. Slam ’n Jam shot-clock readability and other cameras, plus affected SSF2T and UMK3 stages, still need gameplay retesting. Native PS1 resolution is unchanged. SSF2T edge scenery uses reflected existing artwork.

- Adds game-specific widescreen patches for SSF2T, UMK3 and Slam ’n Jam ’96, alongside the existing Flycast widescreen patch for THPS2. Widescreen can be toggled in display settings.

- Refreshes cached core sources before builds so source changes rebuild the embedded engine.
- Includes touch controls and remappable multiplayer controller support on both platforms.

Validation: all four iOS build logs report success; Windows binaries were packaged from the latest local builds. versions.localizedDescription:
**Build 1.0.11.** Install over the existing **Sonic (2006)** app and keep the bundle ID `com.devz.sonic2006`. The IPA is unsigned and contains no game files or patches.

### Sonic '06 Mod Manager patches (.mlua)
The mod manager has a new **Patches** section for patches written for the Sonic '06 Mod Manager, such as Knuxfan24/Sonic-06-Mod-Manager-Patches (https://github.com/Knuxfan24/Sonic-06-Mod-Manager-Patches).

1. Download that repository as a ZIP and extract it in Files.
2. In the mod manager, tap **Import folder** and select the extracted folder.
3. Tap the patches you want, then tap **Play**.

Patches run at launch on top of your mods. The installed game is never modified. Edited files go to `mod-cache/patches` and are reused until you change the selection.

**What works:** patches that edit archives, packages (`.pkg`) or files, and patches that change *data* in the executable. **39 of the 150** patches in Knuxfan24's collection run, for example Disable Fog, Disable Character Stumble, Disable Hint Rings, Disable Music, E3 Timers, Correct Sonic Jump Animation and Opposite Button Prompts. Another 17 already exist as built-in codes.

**What doesn't (yet):**
- **Patches that rewrite game code** (82 in that collection) can't run, because the game's code is recompiled ahead of time. Each shows the address it would change, and can be ported as a built-in code.
- **Patches that edit Lua scripts as text** (29 of them) need decompiled scripts. The game ships compiled ones.

Both kinds stay listed with the reason, instead of failing silently.

### Validation
The ASan/UBSan mod suite passes. It covers package round trips, edits on compressed and raw archive members, renames, data writes, cache reuse, import, and the file overlay. All 31 real packages from a Sonic '06 mod re-serialise byte for byte. The Knuxfan24 collection classifies as 39 runnable out of 150. The Release arm64 iPhoneOS build and the IPA checks passed. Not yet played on a device with patches enabled.

- **Mod manager:** a mod's "can't be enabled" reason no longer spills into the next row. Rows now grow to fit the text.

### New
- **Floating stick.** The movement stick stays hidden until your thumb touches the lower left of the screen, then appears right under it and follows your thumb. Let go and it disappears. Tap **EDIT → STICK** to switch back to the fixed stick with its D-Pad ring. Resizing the stick in the editor also sets the floating stick's size.
- **120 FPS cap.** The game now runs at up to 120 FPS on ProMotion iPhones and iPads, and never above that. The old 60 FPS cap code is gone. If your frame rate was still at the old default of 60, it moves to 120 once. You can lower it any time under **Options → Frame Rate**. Upstream warns that frame rates other than 60 can cause glitches in places, and 120 FPS makes the phone warmer.

- **Stretched touch buttons after switching apps or taking a screenshot.** iOS kept reporting the screen as portrait, and the buttons were drawn several times too tall. They now follow the orientation the game is drawn in.

**Build 1.0.11.** Install over the existing **Sonic (2006)** app and keep the bundle ID `com.devz.sonic2006`. The IPA is unsigned and contains no game files or patches.

The mod manager has a new **Patches** section for patches written for the Sonic '06 Mod Manager, such as Knuxfan24/Sonic-06-Mod-Manager-Patches (https://github.com/Knuxfan24/Sonic-06-Mod-Manager-Patches).

1. Download that repository as a ZIP and extract it in Files.
2. In the mod manager, tap **Import folder** and select the extracted folder.
3. Tap the patches you want, then tap **Play**.

Patches run at launch on top of your mods. The installed game is never modified. Edited files go to `mod-cache/patches` and are reused until you change the selection.

**What works:** patches that edit archives, packages (`.pkg`) or files, and patches that change *data* in the executable. **39 of the 150** patches in Knuxfan24's collection run, for example Disable Fog, Disable Character Stumble, Disable Hint Rings, Disable Music, E3 Timers, Correct Sonic Jump Animation and Opposite Button Prompts. - **Patches that rewrite game code** (82 in that collection) can't run, because the game's code is recompiled ahead of time. Each shows the address it would change, and can be ported as a built-in code.

Bundle ID: `com.devz.nfsu2` · Version: **0.3**, build **2**.

### Mobile experience

- Fullscreen landscape play with optional aspect-fit presentation.
- Uncapped presentation by default; optional FPS ceiling through `NFSU2_FPS_LIMIT`.
- 4× internal width and height by default on iOS; adjustable render scale.
- Racing-style touch controls and a separate simple menu layout. Both layouts support independent positioning, size, opacity, visibility and button mappings, with Save, Cancel and Reset.
- Automatic PAL Menu/Drive switching, including pause/options/frontend detection. A manual toggle remains available.
- Physical controllers take over from the touch pad; disconnecting restores neutral touch input.
- MP3 import from Files, persistent playlist, playback switch, volume and Next Track. Lower the original soundtrack's Music volume in-game to hear only your playlist with game effects.
- Background suspension for the game, GPU work and audio.

### Import and distribution

- Streaming Xbox ISO extraction with path/bounds checks, executable preflight, staged replacement and save preservation.
- PAL Europe and NTSC-U executable profiles. Each build contains one matching executable translation; region-neutral ISO extraction does not provide universal regional playback.
- Active extracted directory and compiled profile shown under **Edit → Game files**. Default directory: **Files → On My iPhone/iPad → NFSU2 → game**.
- New game-cover icon, display name **NFSU2**, bundle ID **com.devz.nfsu2**, version **0.3**, build **2**.
- Public unsigned PAL IPA and SHA-256 checksum in `dist/`; sign for your own device before installation.
- Public source cleaned of local developer notes and compiled test binaries. Game files, generated game code, music and signing material remain excluded from source.

### Performance

- Cache Metal uniform, constant-buffer, texture and sampler bindings within their valid encoder lifetime.
- Reuse unchanged transform-constant uploads within a command buffer; keep fresh allocations for changed constants and instanced draws.
- Combine matching feedback-stage snapshots into one copy per draw.
- Use render-pass clears for complete surface clears while preserving partial and active-pass behavior.
- Native PAL CRT/video conversion fast paths and Apple generated-code optimization.
- Add asynchronous GPU timing diagnostics without waiting for GPU completion.

### Validation and limitations

- Seven input/pacing tests passed, alongside UIKit layout/customization/lifecycle/import tests, MP3 playback tests, XISO checks and Metal GPU regression checks at native and 4× scale.
- Installed and launched on an iPhone 16 Pro Max. All 191 transferred disc files matched source sizes and SHA-1 checksums on-device.
- Synthetic constant-upload benchmarks reduced CPU submission time by about 7–9% for that workload; this is not a measured gameplay FPS gain.
- Real race/pause automatic transitions and sustained gameplay performance still need device validation. Arbitrary regions and executable revisions require their own verified translation.

iOS build 8 · Windows x64 · iOS 16 or later

- Add the NewPixie CRT filter on iOS and Windows. Enable or disable CRT FILTER from the iOS Display menu or Windows pause menu.

- Preserve the original pixel display with CRT off, and reset feedback when toggling or switching widescreen frame sizes.

- Fix Windows Xbox input by reading buttons, sticks and triggers through XInput. Gameplay, controller setup and menus use the same polled input state.
- Improve iOS controller event delivery, including Menu/Start and gamepad routing on iOS 18 and later.
- Keep controller slots stable across reordering and disconnects. Controllers join as Player 1, Player 3, Player 2 and Player 4.
- Align Player 1 and Player 4 possession indicators and scoring flashes with their status plates.
- Restore camera tracking at both near-side corners. Limit the inbound view separately so it stays inside the available scenery at both court ends.
- Preserve live settings changes, including switching head size during gameplay. Normal, big and huge head settings apply to all four players.
- Strip private build paths and debug metadata from release binaries. Check packages for ROMs, signing credentials and development artifacts.

- `NBA-Hangtime-Windows-x64.zip`
- `NBA-Hangtime-iOS.ipa` (unsigned; sign using your sideloading tool)
- `NBA-Hangtime-0.4.3-source.zip`

# Sonic Unleashed for iOS v1.1.0 — Native Mod Manager

## Changelog

- Added a native startup mod manager with folder import through Files.
- Enable or disable mods, reorder priority, and preserve selections across launches.
- Check dependency IDs and minimum numeric versions before starting.
- Toggle the built-in game codes from the manager.
- Connect selections to the existing asset replacements, append archives, loose files, UMM merges, and mod save redirection.
- Display unsupported DLL and custom HMM script requirements.
- Confine mod include/save paths and reject symbolic links.
- Compile the game Metal shader cache for iOS 15 with the iPhone SDK.
- Target iOS 15 for bundled dependencies and use numeric bundle versions.
- Add an IPA packaging helper for builds made with the Ninja preset.

## Install and use

Download `SonicUnleashed_iOS_v1.1.0.ipa` and re-sign it with your sideloading tool before installation. This IPA has an ad-hoc signature and no Apple provisioning profile. Supply your own runtime game assets through Files.

Extract an Unleashed Recompiled mod, launch the app, tap **Import folder**, and select the folder containing `mod.ini`. Enable it, set its priority, and tap **Play**. New imports start disabled. The first mod wins file replacement conflicts.

## MCX360 Edition 1.1

### New
- **On-screen touch controls**, using the layout from the XeniOS emulator. They show when no controller is connected and hide when one connects. Adjust them with `touch_controls`, `touch_controls_opacity` and `touch_haptics` in `mc360.toml`.
- **Save thumbnails**: your worlds now show a picture in the world list.
- **Exit Game** now closes the app instead of leaving a black screen.

### Performance
- Much lower CPU load while playing. The game's threads no longer queue up on a shared lock, calls inside the game run directly, and waits end as soon as the GPU is ready instead of sleeping in whole milliseconds.
- Frame rate capped at a steady, evenly paced 60 FPS (`framerate_limit`, default 60).
- The game's main thread and GPU thread now get priority on the iPhone's performance cores.
- Less heat: the game no longer spins a core at full power while waiting for the GPU, and no longer copies the whole screen image back and forth several times per frame.

### Fixes
- Fixed random crashes after playing for a while.
- Fixed choppy audio.
- Fixed "ghost" blocks and old terrain showing where the world had changed.
- Devices with 3 GB of RAM now show an explanation at launch instead of crashing.

### Known issues
- Long sessions heat the phone, and iOS then slows it down, so the frame rate can drop over time. Playing unplugged and without a case helps.
- The on-screen D-pad's up arrow sits over the first world's thumbnail in the Load menu. It's part of the controls, not the save.
- Devices with 3 GB of RAM (iPhone 8 Plus, iPhone X, iPad 8th gen) can't run the game with a normal sideload. They need TrollStore, or a signing method that grants the Extended Virtual Addressing entitlement.

Installing over 1.0 keeps your worlds and settings.
First iOS release.
